title: Block close: character is daily
hookLine: the traits are built one day at a time

cards: A jar of sourdough starter sits on a kitchen counter. Flour and water, a little bubbly, a little sour. Its keeper feeds it every day.
Skip a day, and it sulks. Skip a week, and it may not come back. No feeding is big enough to last a month.
The starter lives on small, steady care, and in return it raises every loaf. Mussar treats character much the same way.

teach.b: First, the map. This block walked through traits as measures, each with a right size: humility, patience, gratitude, order, calm, silence, truth, trust, zeal, generosity, honor, responsibility.
Then speech: harmful speech, tales, slander, and speaking good. Then the hard ones, anger and envy, and Luzzatto's ladder up to holiness.
Then ethics in the world: honest weights, not stealing minds, fair work, animals, waste, and the open tent. Second, repetition.

teach.h: PRACTICE THE OPPOSITE, AGAIN AND AGAIN.
teach.b: Maimonides, in his laws of character, says that a person who wants to change a trait should practice the opposite act, again and again, until it comes easily and becomes part of who they are. Not a vow. A habit.
Third, a thousand coins. The Mishnah, in Ethics of the Fathers, says the world is judged by the abundance of deeds.
Maimonides, commenting on it, gives an example: someone who gives a thousand coins to one person at one time doesn't build generosity the way someone does who gives one coin a thousand times.
The trait grows from the number of acts, not the size of one. Fourth, no finish line.

teach.h: NOT YOURS TO COMPLETE, NOT FREE TO STOP.
teach.b: Rabbi Tarfon says, in the same tractate, that it isn't yours to complete the work, and you aren't free to stop doing it.
That's why Mussar, as this block met it, meant one trait at a time, an accounting of the soul at night, and beginning again the next morning. None of these traits is learned in a day.
Every one of them is learned daily.

how: In a Mussar group, a student may choose one trait to work on for a set stretch of time, practice a small daily act tied to it, and keep a short nightly journal of how the day went.

o: a look back: character is built one act at a time
a vow to master every trait in a single month
a final test you must pass before moving on

games.q: character is daily — tap the pairs.
p: practice the opposite until it's easy
not yours to complete, not free to stop

s: for Maimonides, a trait changes mainly through one strong vow
he says to practice the opposite act again and again until it becomes part of you.
Maimonides says one coin given a thousand times builds generosity more than a thousand coins at once
in his commentary on the Mishnah, the trait grows from the number of acts.
Rabbi Tarfon says you must finish the work before you rest
he says it isn't yours to complete it, and you aren't free to stop.

games.q: you want to become generous. you have a thousand coins to give. which way builds the trait, according to Maimonides?
o: give all thousand to one person at once.
give one coin at a time, a thousand times.
save them until you can give more.
games.why: Maimonides says the trait grows from the number of acts, not the size of one gift: one coin a thousand times.

practice: Let the traits from this block pass by: humility, patience, gratitude, truth, generosity, calm, speaking good, honest dealing, an open door.

Notice which one tugs, not the most impressive but the one your days actually need, and choose it for the month ahead, shrunk to one small daily act: one thank-you, one honest sentence, one coin, one pause before answering.
If you pray, ask for help with it in your own words.

wordCard.voice: Block close. Mussar and Jewish ethics: traits, speech, the ladder, and the world, built one act at a time. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: character is daily. Next comes a new block: the life cycle, from birth to death. A block done, one day at a time.

sources.ref: Mishneh Torah, Laws of Character (Hilchot De'ot) 1:7 and 2:2
Maimonides, Commentary on the Mishnah, Avot 3:15
